expects.rule: Show prices. When a B2B offer is too configurable to price exactly, show sample prices for typical cases rather than nothing; Nielsen called missing prices on B2B sites the number one web design mistake of 2002.
Plans sit side by side as cards with the price, the billing unit (per user, per month) and one primary button each; three to four plans, with the enterprise plan using a separate contact action.
A monthly and yearly toggle states the saving as a number or percentage, and the default is visible.
A feature comparison table follows the cards, and its plan headers stay visible while the visitor scrolls.
Usage-based prices give exact rates (for example a percentage plus a fixed fee) and an example or a calculator.
An FAQ under the table answers billing, refunds, seats, limits and taxes in plain sentences.
The recommended plan is marked once, and the free tier or trial states what is limited.

traits: Plan cards or columns sit in one row on 7 of 7 pages: four on Linear, Slack and Plausible, three on Twenty and Figma, and Notion's cards are 3 plus Enterprise.
Prices are real figures with currency and unit on 6 of 7; Stripe gives percentage-plus-fixed-fee rates; Enterprise shows Custom or a contact button on 5 of 7.
A billing toggle (monthly or yearly) is present on 5 of 7 (Linear, Notion, Figma, Plausible, Twenty), placed above or inside the cards, and 3 of those state the saving (20%, 2 months free, -25%).
The title is 32 to 72px on 7 of 7 and takes one to three lines; 3 of 7 are left-aligned (Linear, Stripe, Figma).
A plan is flagged on 2 of 7 (Notion Recommended, Slack Best value); the others mark none.
One typeface family per page on 7 of 7 (Twenty adds a mono for labels and Notion a serif for 1% of text).
Customer logos appear between title and plans on 2 of 7 (Notion, Slack); cookie banners cover part of the first screen on 4 of 7.

sites.name: Linear
sites.why: Near-black page (#08090a), a 48px title, then four plan columns (Free $0, Basic $10, Business $16 per user per month, Enterprise Custom) each with a feature checklist; a Billed yearly switch sits inside the paid plans. Get started and Contact sales buttons at the foot of the columns. All in Inter. Comparison table below.

sites.name: Twenty
sites.why: Light grey page, a two-line serif title (Simple Pricing), a Monthly / Yearly -25% switch and a Self-hosting checkbox, then three cards: Pro $9 per user per month, Organization $39 outlined in blue, Enterprise from $50k per year, each with small illustrations. Nav includes a GitHub stars count.

avoid: No prices at all and a single Contact sales button for every plan.
Three identical cards with different checkmark lists and no billing unit, so the real cost per user is unclear.
A comparison table of icons only, with no text on what each limit is.
A toggle that defaults to the yearly price without saying that the price is billed yearly.
Dark patterns: countdowns that reset, a pre-selected paid add-on, or a free plan hidden in small grey text.
Plan names that do not tell who each plan is for (Basic, Plus, Pro, Ultra, Max) with no description line.
